function: Joint learned control of BS transmit power, UAV-RIS horizontal placement, RIS phase shifts and per-element information-transmission time, maximizing energy efficiency under jamming (p. 6).
system: BS with 8 antennas, 3 single-antenna users, single-antenna jammer, UAV-mounted passive reflecting RIS (20-70 elements, energy harvesting), 2 GHz, 10 MHz (pp. 3, 4, 10).
method: Model-free deep reinforcement learning, HER-SD3: softmax double deep deterministic policy gradient actor-critic with hindsight experience replay; trained by interaction with the simulated environment (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Own simulator, no standard model or measurements: BS-RIS path loss 17log10(d)+68.8 with Rician fading (K=31.3); RIS-user LoS/NLoS air-to-ground model of [37] (pp. 4, 5, 9, 10).
test_conditions: One simulated 200x200x100 m scenario with moving users and jammer; no separate test scenario, only sweeps of RIS elements, BS power and jamming power (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Learned only: SD3-based UAV-RIS [34], TD3, and HER-SD3 with fixed UAV-RIS location (variant of the proposed method); no classical or non-learned baseline (pp. 10-13).
metrics: Energy efficiency (Mbps/J), harvested energy (J), average throughput (Mbps), average reward and convergence speed in training episodes (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Order of complexity O(IT(sum of actor and critic layer neuron products + log2 D)) for I episodes and T steps; no runtime or parameter count (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 5: "low-altitude aerial platform communication model considering both LoS and NLoS factors" is the RIS-user channel; p. 4: BS-RIS link uses path loss with "Rician fading". Custom simulator, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "varies from 20 to 70" is a sweep of the number of RIS elements inside one simulated scenario; the paper never states that a trained model is tested in an unseen scenario or after adaptation.
q3_support: p. 10: "denoted by SD3-Based UAV-RIS [34]" and "HER-SD3-Based Fixed-RIS" plus TD3 are the only comparisons (Figs. 4-7, pp. 11-13); all learned or a variant of the proposed method, no non-learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 9: "Hence, the computational complexity of the HER approach is O(log2 D)." Subsection C also gives the total order of HER-SD3 as O(IT(... + log2 D)) for I episodes and T steps.
q5_support: p. 10: "The partial training parameters considered for the simulation are provided in Table II"; own simulator, and no link to code or data appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Area 6 chosen because the links are aerial (BS to UAV-mounted RIS to maritime users) and the agent controls power, RIS phase shifts and placement jointly (p. 6); area 3 is the alternative if the reviewer treats the UAV only as the platform of the RIS, since area 6 wins the tie by specificity. Function check: anti-jamming is the objective (title, p. 1), but the learned action is BS power, RIS phase shifts, RIS scheduling and UAV placement (p. 6), so it solves the problem of area 3 or 6. The above_phy check passes because the UAV placement is learned jointly with power and RIS phase. The RIS-user model of [37] (p. 5) is an academic analytical air-to-ground model, not a 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model, so q1 is 0; the reviewer may confirm. Table II on p. 10 is an image and lists only partial parameters. Training and testing are not separated: results are from the same environment, so q2 is 0.
